question: When and where is the Open House?
answer: Saturday, October 17, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Start at the Mechanical Engineering booth in the VVC gym, catch the program presentation at 10:00 AM in ETLC L1-001, then tour the Mechanical Engineering Building from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM. The Map page shows the way.

question: Do I need to register or buy a ticket?
answer: No, registration is not required for the Mechanical Engineering Open House. You can simply drop by and explore. If you choose to register for the University of Alberta Open House, you'll also be entered to win prizes when you check in on event day.

question: Who is the Open House for?
answer: Future students, their families, and anyone curious about Mechanical Engineering at the University of Alberta are welcome to attend!

question: Can parents, guardians or friends come along?
answer: Yes! Everyone is welcome to join the tour.

question: Can I take transit?
answer: Yes. Plan your trip to the University of Alberta with the ETS Trip Planner.

question: How do I get from the VVC gym to the Mechanical Engineering Building?
answer: It's about an 8-minute walk. Open Map → Getting here for the walking route, then enter the building on the 1st floor and take the stairs beside room 1-3A up to the 2nd floor, where the tour starts.

question: How long does the building tour take?
answer: The building tour runs from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM on a drop-in basis, so you can come and go anytime during those hours.

question: Is the building accessible?
answer: Elevators are next to the stairs on each floor and are marked on the tour map.

question: Where are the washrooms?
answer: Washrooms are marked on each floor of the tour map with the washroom icon.

question: Is there food or water available?
answer: There will be plenty of places to purchase food and drinks on campus (times vary):
list: Food trucks near the Flag Plaza outside University Commons
Starbucks in Cameron Library, Kipnes Academy and CCIS
footer: Tip: turn on Food on the Map page to see them all.

question: How does the passport work?
answer: Scan the QR code at each station with the Scan button to collect its sticker. There are 14 stickers: 2 on campus and 12 inside the Mechanical Engineering Building. Your passport shows which ones you still need.

question: My phone won't scan the QR code. What should I do?
answer: Allow camera access when your browser asks, hold the phone steady about 20 to 30 cm from the code, and make sure it's well lit. You can also scan with your phone's camera app. If it still won't work, ask a volunteer at the station.

question: Is there a prize for collecting every sticker?
answer: Collect all 14 to earn the Certified Explorer seal.

question: Will I lose my stickers if I close the page?
answer: No. Your passport is saved in this browser on this device, so you can close the page and come back. It won't carry over to another phone or browser, and clearing your browser data or using a private window will erase it.

question: Do I need an account? Is my information collected?
answer: No account is needed. Your collected stickers are stored only on your own device and are never sent to us.

question: Who can I ask for help during the event?
answer: Look for the wayfinding tents at these locations:
list: Main Quad, close to the Centennial Centre for Interdisciplinary Science (CCIS)
Along 89 Avenue between the Students' Union Building (SUB) and the South Academic Building (SAB)
footer: Tip: turn on Help tents on the Map page to find the closest one.
